# RIVERTHREAD OPERA — existing assets and tour records

## Company identity

- Asset: 03-riverthread-wordmark.png
- Complete identity: ribbon emblem, RIVERTHREAD and OPERA lettering
- Colour: deep burgundy, nominal #8A2534
- Source field: white
- Fixed attributes: lettering, emblem, arrangement, proportions and colour
- Permitted transformation: uniform scaling
- Application background: light solid colour
- Visible bounds: complete, clear of other elements
- Image coverage: complete mark on every image deliverable
- Presentation coverage: complete mark within the document; page-level placement varies

## Costume pattern

- Asset: 04-costume-pattern.png
- Source: the company's original stage-costume border pattern
- Elements: gold upright hollow diamonds with central dots, pale wave bands and a deep blue field
- Asset function: motif source for new compositions
- Permitted transformations: cropping, repetition, uniform scaling and placement of fragments
- Fixed attributes: source colours, upright orientation and internal geometry
- Minimum image coverage: one complete upright hollow diamond with its central dot and one recognisable portion of the pale wave band
- Other repeats: partial crops permitted
- Interpretive scope: visual connections within this production

## Production

| Field | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Company | RIVERTHREAD OPERA |
| Production title | The Borrowed Lantern |
| Audience introduction | Story, song and percussion. |
| Performance language | English |
| Duration | 90 minutes, including one 10-minute interval |
| Admission | General admission; unreserved seating |

## Tour stops

| Code | Exact venue | Date | Doors | Performance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AT | Alder Town Hall | 27 February 2027 | 18:30 | 19:00 |
| BA | Bracken Arts House | 6 March 2027 | 14:30 | 15:00 |

## Text treatment

- Required names and fixed lines: original words
- Capitalisation and line breaks: variable
- Dates and times: supplied wording or unambiguous equivalent English format
- Doors and performance: distinct information labels
- Schedule associations: each venue paired with its own record
- Story imagery: original non-portrait imagery

## Original story

Synopsis: A young boat repairer borrows the town's only ceremonial lantern to finish a night repair. When the lantern disappears, a neighbour assumes it was sold. Three encounters across the river reveal a chain of practical kindness. Returning the lantern becomes a shared journey rather than a private apology.

## Newcomer notes

- Voice: character and dialogue
- Percussion: changes in pace and entrances
- Repeated costume motifs: connections between scenes
- Scope: descriptions of The Borrowed Lantern

## Shared audience guide

- Title: Your first visit
- Line 1: Check the venue and performance time on your ticket.
- Line 2: Doors open 30 minutes before the performance.
- Line 3: The performance includes a 10-minute interval.
- Supporting content: production title, complete company mark and required pattern fragment
- Function: general tour guidance

## Material content records

| Material | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Identity specification | #8A2534; complete-mark treatment; upright diamond and wave-band requirement; audience introduction |
| Rules board | Company mark; required pattern fragment; original examples relating both assets to title and practical information |
| Tour key visual | Company mark; required pattern fragment; production title; audience introduction |
| Venue poster, each stop | Company mark; pattern fragment; title; introduction; venue; date; doors; performance; language; duration including interval; admission |
| Sample ticket, each stop | Company mark; pattern fragment; title; venue; date; doors; performance; admission; SAMPLE — NOT VALID FOR ENTRY |
| Programme cover | Company mark; pattern fragment; title; venue; date |
| Programme spread | Company mark; pattern fragment; title; venue; date; full synopsis meaning; three newcomer notes; language; duration including interval |
| Entrance sign, each stop | Company mark; pattern fragment; title; venue; date; Audience entrance; doors; performance |
| Tour announcement video | Key visual; complete company mark; pattern; title; introduction; both venues, dates, doors and performance times |
| Presentation | Earlier work; specification facts; production and asset facts matching these records |

## Programme and presentation scope

- Programme edition: Alder Town Hall, 27 February 2027
- Programme cover count: 1
- Programme spread count: 1
- Spread structure: two pages, landscape overall, visible centre divide
- Essential text placement: contained within individual pages
- Spread item count: two pages together form one item
- Video duration: 10 seconds
- Presentation length: at least 8 pages

## Atmosphere reference

- Asset: 05-backstage-materials.png
- Role: reference
- Subject: stage fabric, wood and warm light
- Relationship to identity: tactile atmosphere

steps.userMessage:
RIVERTHREAD OPERA | A touring identity for The Borrowed Lantern

We are taking The Borrowed Lantern to Alder Town Hall on 27 February 2027 and Bracken Arts House on 6 March 2027. We need a contemporary touring identity that welcomes people encountering our theatre for the first time. Print the company name through the supplied complete mark, "RIVERTHREAD OPERA", and use the audience introduction "Story, song and percussion.". The performance is in English and lasts 90 minutes, including one 10-minute interval. Admission is general admission with unreserved seating. Alder Town Hall opens at 18:30 for a 19:00 performance; Bracken Arts House opens at 14:30 for a 15:00 performance.

The direction starts with our existing assets. Preserve the complete burgundy wordmark and ribbon emblem, nominal colour #8A2534, with their lettering, arrangement and proportions intact. Its permitted treatment is uniform scaling on a light solid background, with its full visible bounds clear of other elements. The costume pattern supplies gold upright hollow diamonds with central dots, pale wave bands and a deep blue field. Cropping, repetition and uniform scaling are its permitted transformations; preserve source colours, orientation and internal geometry. Every image deliverable must carry the complete mark and a pattern fragment containing at least one complete upright diamond with its central dot and one recognisable portion of the pale wave band. Develop materials for both stops, with the programme cover and spread prepared for the Alder Town Hall opening.

Audience: first-time opera audiences choosing a performance and preparing for their visit, and our touring and venue teams approving the public materials.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the fixed asset treatments, production records, synopsis and audience guidance. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable with its proportion, format and stage. 03-riverthread-wordmark.png is the identity input containing the complete company mark. 04-costume-pattern.png is the constraint input defining the existing costume motif's colours and geometry. 05-backstage-materials.png is an atmosphere reference for the tactile relationship between stage fabric, wood and warm light.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page identity specification recording #8A2534, the complete-mark treatment, the upright diamond and wave-band requirement, and the audience introduction Story, song and percussion.
2. One rules board with the supplied mark and pattern, title treatments, and practical-information examples distinguishing doors from performance times
3. One tour key visual with the complete mark, pattern fragment, The Borrowed Lantern and Story, song and percussion.
4. Two venue posters, one per stop, with the mark, pattern, production title, audience introduction, venue, date, doors and performance times, English language, 90-minute duration including the 10-minute interval, and general admission with unreserved seating
5. Two sample tickets, one per stop, with the mark, pattern, title, venue, date, doors and performance times, admission status and the printed label "SAMPLE — NOT VALID FOR ENTRY"
6. One Alder Town Hall programme cover with the mark, pattern, production title, venue and 27 February 2027
7. One Alder Town Hall programme spread comprising two landscape pages with a visible centre divide, the mark, pattern, title, venue, date, English language, duration including interval, the complete plot outline and three newcomer notes
8. Two entrance signs, one per stop, with the mark, pattern, title, venue, date, doors and performance times, and the heading "Audience entrance"
9. One shared audience guide headed "Your first visit", with the mark, pattern, production title and the three visit-guidance lines supplied below
10. One 10-second tour announcement video using the key visual, complete mark, pattern, production title, audience introduction and both stops' venue, date, doors and performance information
11. One presentation document of at least 8 pages, reusing the specification, rules board, key visual, both stops' posters, tickets and signs, the programme cover and spread, audience guide and video stills

Acceptance:
- Establish the identity specification before the rules board and applications. On the rules board, tour key visual, both venue posters and presentation, repeat its complete-mark treatment, upright diamond and wave-band requirement, and Story, song and percussion. Print #8A2534 in the specification and presentation.
- On the rules board, key visual, posters, tickets, programme cover and spread, entrance signs and audience guide, preserve the complete RIVERTHREAD OPERA mark through uniform scaling on a light solid background. Use the pattern in its source colours and upright geometry, with at least one complete hollow diamond, its central dot and a recognisable pale wave-band portion in each image.
- On both venue posters, sample tickets, entrance signs and the video, pair Alder Town Hall with 27 February 2027, doors 18:30 and performance 19:00, and Bracken Arts House with 6 March 2027, doors 14:30 and performance 15:00. Label doors and performance separately. Print SAMPLE — NOT VALID FOR ENTRY on both tickets and Audience entrance on both signs; carry the same schedules into the presentation wherever a stop is described.
- On the programme cover and spread, use Alder Town Hall and 27 February 2027. In the spread, retain the young boat repairer's borrowing, the lantern's disappearance, the neighbour's belief that it was sold, three encounters across the river revealing practical kindness, and the shared return. Present three notes explaining how this production uses voice for character and dialogue, percussion for pace changes and entrances, and repeated costume motifs for connections between scenes. Place each text block within one page of the spread.
- On the audience guide, print Your first visit and the exact lines "Check the venue and performance time on your ticket.", "Doors open 30 minutes before the performance." and "The performance includes a 10-minute interval.". On both posters and the programme spread, state English and 90 minutes, including one 10-minute interval; on both posters and tickets, state general admission and unreserved seating.
- Deliver a 10-second video with a separately readable information sequence for each of the two stops. In the presentation's minimum 8 pages, reuse every earlier deliverable, with video stills representing the announcement, and identify how the rules board's title and practical-information hierarchy carries into the posters, tickets and entrance signs.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
